lede: Jon had the best week anyone has had all season — four teams, four wins — and it did exactly what it should have: Mark's lead went from four points to two. Mark's 49ers closing on Monday night is the only reason it is not one. Underneath them the table compressed too, with Harrison, Patrick and Brian separated by a point and a half and Bill blanked.

beats.text: Two points, and they were the two that kept this from getting uncomfortable. San Francisco beat Washington 23-17 on Monday to go 6-0, building a 20-3 half behind two Christian McCaffrey touchdowns and holding on after Jayden Daniels threw for 300. Chicago won in Atlanta with Caleb Williams back from the hamstring and 30-of-36. The other half of his week was losses — Baltimore fell 13-10 in Cleveland without Lamar Jackson, Las Vegas lost to Jon — and a four-point lead is now two.

beats.tag: Jon · Four for four, and it counted
beats.text: The Titans won their first game of the season in Indianapolis, down thirteen at half with sixty-four yards of offense, on a blocked punt and two late Joey Slye field goals. Pittsburgh came back from 16-3 to win in overtime. Kansas City handled the Chargers. Buffalo beat Mark in Las Vegas, where Josh Allen tied Jim Kelly's franchise record of 258 touchdown passes. Four from four — the third sweep of the season and the first since Mark in Week 3 — and the deficit went from four to two.

beats.tag: The chase · A point and a half
beats.text: Harrison took New England and Houston and lost Washington on Monday, finishing on 12.5. Patrick had Cleveland's last-second win over Baltimore and Carolina's over Philadelphia, which puts him on 12. Brian got Jacksonville's loss in London but New Orleans' thirty-four unanswered against the Giants, and sits on 11. Three owners, a point and a half, and all three play twice against the top two in Week 7.

Green Bay beat Dallas 23-13 on Sunday night, which was both Zach's only point and Bill's whole problem. The Packers led wire to wire, converted their first seven third downs, and Dak Prescott threw interceptions on back-to-back drives inside the Green Bay 30. Bill finished 0 for 3 — the Giants, the Buccaneers and the Cowboys all lost, with Cincinnati on bye — and is the only owner who came out of Week 6 with nothing.

New England at Chicago, and it is Harrison against Mark again four days after the last one. Both teams are 4-2. Caleb Williams is off the injury report entirely; the Patriots lost three offensive linemen during the Jets game and play on a short week against a front that sacked Michael Penix Jr. five times. Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve with a blood clot and Lamar Jackson's ankle is still day to day — two of the four teams at the top of this league have a quarterback question going into the weekend.
